[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-10.30): Good afternoon, Adrian. Rachel Tan here. Thanks for setting aside time for our telephone appointment. Are you somewhere comfortable to speak privately?
[seg_0002] Client (10.70-18.90): Hi Rachel. Yes, I'm in my office with the door closed. Telephone appointments are easier for me than coming down, especially between meetings.
[seg_0003] Advisor (19.30-28.06): Of course. We can keep this concise. Before we begin, could you provide your identification particulars for the usual verification?
[seg_0004] Client (28.46-39.38): My FIN is F zero zero seven zero five eight five Q. My date of birth is 16 April 1978. I've got a little breathing space now; my next business appointment is later.
[seg_0005] Advisor (39.78-58.10): Thank you. It's helpful to have a quiet slot rather than fit personal administration in while you're rushing. Your investment objective is to build a diversified portfolio focused on income and steadier performance, rather than aggressive growth. I'll use that as the basis for our discussion.
[seg_0006] Client (58.50-68.00): I usually put these appointments in my diary, same as business meetings. Otherwise the paperwork just sits there. The fund I want to invest in is Harbor SGD Bond Fund.
[seg_0007] Advisor (68.39-97.00): I'll keep the discussion straightforward. I recommend Harbor SGD Bond Fund because its pooled fixed-income holdings support your income objective and spread exposure across issuers, rather than concentrating it with an individual issuer. For Harbor SGD Bond Fund, rising market interest rates can push down the value of the bonds it holds, which can lower the fund's value. Do you understand how rising interest rates could lower the value of this fund?
[seg_0008] Client (97.40-104.94): Yes, I understand. If interest rates rise, the bonds held by the fund can fall in value, and my fund investment can fall too.
[seg_0009] Advisor (105.34-119.14): The transaction charge is 0.5% of the investment amount. You could lose some or even all of the capital you invest in this fund. Having heard those risks, are you willing to accept investment losses on this investment?
[seg_0010] Client (119.54-139.42): Yes, I am willing to accept investment losses and fluctuations in the fund's value. I understand the risks you've explained. My existing holding is denominated in Chinese yuan, but that's separate from this new investment. My overall account value is 1,200,000 in Singapore dollars. That's portfolio context, not the amount I'm investing today.
[seg_0011] Advisor (139.82-152.99): An allocation of 25,000 in Singapore dollars would just be an illustration for our sizing discussion, not your actual transaction amount. I'll leave a pause here so you have room to speak without me interrupting.
[seg_0012] Client (153.39-168.50): For this transaction, please use Singapore dollars. The amount I'm committing to this investment is 500,000. The quantity I want for this transaction is 1,500 units. I want to buy the fund units to add to my portfolio. Please place this as a market order.
[seg_0013] Advisor (168.90-172.91): Let me read back the direction: you want to sell the fund units.
[seg_0014] Client (173.31-177.70): No, I said buy. I'm adding to my investment, not disposing of it.
[seg_0015] Advisor (178.10-198.84): Sorry about that, Adrian. Thank you for catching my mistake. With the direction corrected, your final instruction is to buy 1,500 units of Harbor SGD Bond Fund, with an investment amount of 500,000 in Singapore dollars, using a market order. Do you explicitly confirm that final instruction?
[seg_0016] Client (199.24-204.25): Yes, I confirm that final transaction instruction as you've just stated it. Please proceed.
[seg_0017] Advisor (204.65-212.49): Thank you. For any routine follow-up, would you prefer a telephone appointment again, or an email to arrange a suitable slot?
[seg_0018] Client (212.89-219.92): An email to arrange the slot is best. During the workday I may not pick up an unexpected call, but a planned appointment is easy enough.
[seg_0019] Advisor (220.32-228.78): Noted. We'll use that approach for scheduling. Thanks for your time today, Adrian. I'll let you get back to your afternoon.
[seg_0020] Client (229.18-234.25): Thanks, Rachel. Appreciate keeping it brief. Have a good afternoon, bye.

MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE  18 
5 PRICING CONTROLS AND DISCLOSURES 
 
5.1 PBs should establish requirements for RMs to provide clients with adequate 
pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should

documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.

account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
